title: Sale of Minor's Property Without Court Permission in Bangladesh: Legal Validity, Section 29 & Buyer Remedies
metaTitle: Sale of Minor's Property in Bangladesh | Court Permission Rules
metaDescription: Is selling a minor's land legal in Bangladesh without District Judge Court permission? Section 29 & 30 Guardians and Wards Act 1890 explained by Supreme Court Lawyer.
keywords: minor land sale without court permission
district judge court permission minor property
heroIntro: Selling, transferring, or mortgaging property belonging to a minor (a person under 18 years of age) is strictly governed by the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 and the Majority Act 1875 in Bangladesh. A common trap for property buyers is purchasing land from parents or relatives acting as natural guardians without obtaining prior permission from the competent District Judge Court. Under Advocate Md. Shah Alam's legal guidance, this article clarifies the legal consequences, voidability of such deeds under Section 30, and how buyers and minor heirs can protect their lawful rights. quickAnswer.heading: ⚡ Key Takeaways: Minor's Property Sale Laws (2026)
points: Even a father or mother cannot sell a minor child's immovable property without prior statutory permission from the District Judge Court.
Any sale deed executed without court sanction is voidable under Section 30 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 at the instance of the minor upon attaining majority.
The limitation period for a minor to challenge and cancel an unauthorized sale deed is 3 years from the date of turning 18.
Before purchasing inherited family property with minor co-heirs, insist on an official Guardianship Certificate and Sale Permission Order.

sections.heading: 1. Who Qualifies as a Legal Guardian under Bangladeshi Law?
sections.content: Under Muslim Law and the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, the father is the primary legal guardian of the person and property of a minor. Upon the father's death, the paternal grandfather or a guardian appointed by the father's registered will acts as legal guardian. The mother is considered the natural custodian (Hizanat) but does not have automatic legal power to dispose of the minor's immovable property unless appointed by the District Judge.

sections.heading: 2. Section 29: Mandatory District Judge Permission for Selling Minor Property
sections.content: Section 29 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890 explicitly restricts court-appointed guardians from mortgaging, charging, or transferring by sale, gift, or exchange any part of the minor's immovable property without previous permission of the Court. The District Judge grants permission only upon proof of necessity or evident advantage for the minor's welfare, education, or maintenance.

sections.heading: 3. Section 30: Legal Consequences of Unauthorized Sale (Voidable Deeds)
sections.content: Under Section 30, any disposal of immovable property by a guardian in contravention of Section 28 or Section 29 is voidable at the option of the minor or any person affected thereby. The deed is not void ab initio, but the minor can repudiate the transfer without refunding the consideration unless the buyer proves the funds were genuinely applied for the minor's benefit.

sections.heading: 4. How a Minor Can Cancel Fraudulent Deeds Upon Attaining 18 Years
sections.content: When a minor turns 18, they can file a Declaration and Deed Cancellation Suit (Specific Relief Act Section 39) before the Joint District Judge Court. Under Article 44 of the Limitation Act 1908, the suit must be instituted within 3 years from the date of attaining majority (i.e., before reaching 21 years of age).

sections.heading: 5. Step-by-Step Procedure to Obtain Court Permission to Sell Minor's Land
sections.content:
1. Guardian Appointment Petition: File an application under Section 10 of Act VIII of 1890 before the District Judge.
  2. Valuation & Assessment: Submit updated Mouza rate and estimated price schedule.
  3. Justification of Benefit: Prove legitimate cause (e.g., educational expenses, medical treatment, or purchasing higher-yielding property).
  4. Court Order & Conditional Deed Execution: The Court issues a conditional order mandating the sale proceeds to be deposited into a judicial fixed-deposit account for the minor.

sections.heading: 6. Essential Checklist for Buyers Purchasing Inherited Family Lands
sections.content:
• Check the age of all co-heirs on the Warishan certificate.
  • If any heir is under 18, demand a certified copy of the District Judge's Sale Permission Order.
  • Verify that the deed reflects the exact schedule of land approved by the court.
  • Ensure the guardian signs strictly in their representative capacity under court authority.

sections.heading: 7. FAQs & Supreme Court Land Specialist Consultation
sections.content:
Q: Can a mother sell her minor children's land after the father's death?
A: No. A mother cannot legally execute a sale deed for her minor children's share without obtaining an order of guardianship and specific permission from the District Judge Court.

faq.question: What happens if I buy land from a minor's guardian without court permission?
faq.answer: The deed remains legally precarious. Once the minor turns 18, they can sue to cancel the deed and recover possession under Section 30 of the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.

faq.question: How long does it take to get court permission to sell a minor's land in Bangladesh?
faq.answer: Generally 2 to 4 months before the District Judge Court, including notice publication and verification of the minor's welfare.
